text:
maria: Heads up — automated healthwatch flagged sustained growth in DRAM ECC correctable errors on GPU card 13 in usw1-pool7 (host: gpu-usw1-7-3). Counters: correctable +1200 over 6h. Opening triage.

devon: Can you paste the nvml/dmesg excerpt? Any Xid errors?

maria: Here's the nvml extract:
```
GPU 13: Correctable ECC errors: 1256
Uncorrectable ECC errors: 0
nvidia-smi -q -d ERROR shows growing ce_count in memory
Kernel dmesg: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31
```

li: That pattern (rapid CE growth without UE yet) is classic for a row remap in progress — we should prepare for page retirement. Keep an eye on Xid 31 — can be precursor.

ops-bot: incident-bot created ticket INF-8642: gpu-usw1-7-3 card13 memory-error-growth (linked)

maria: No UEs so far. Workload was a long-context generation test; sequence lengths spiked. I've dumped perf counters and uploaded logs: s3://redwood-ops/diag/INF-8642/

devon: Capacity impact? That card is part of a node backing dedicated pool7 (8 GPUs/node). Draining node will drop pool throughput by ~12.5% for that node. Need coordination with Dedicated product.

amanda: Suggest soft-shedding: mark GPU as degraded in scheduler, route new sessions away, keep existing ones to finish.

maria: Plan: at 02:00 UTC I'll cordon the node and drain with graceful 10m timeout. Command I'll run:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-usw1-7-3
kubectl drain gpu-usw1-7-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=600
```

li: After drain, run vendor health tools to attempt remap and issue page retirement. If remap fails, tag for RMA. Add asset tag 'gpu:needs-rma'.

ops-bot: asset-db updated: gpu-usw1-7-3.card13 tags: [gpu:needs-rma]

devon: If we see any uncorrectable ECC (UE) or Xid increases post-drain, initiate immediate power-cycle and open vendor escalation (support@vendor).

maria: Notifying oncall and Dedicated PMs. I'll post an update after the drain. :thumbsup:

li: Also add this card to the long-term tracker (gpu-fault-tracker) so we can correlate with other pool7 incidents.

maria: Update: drain scheduled, ticket INF-8642 created, logs in S3. Will follow up with remediation steps and capacity impact note.
